You are auditing a Next.js 16 + Prisma 7 + NextAuth v5 app called antri-capil, deployed on Vercel
at https://antri-capil.vercel.app for Disdukcapil Kabupaten Sambas, Indonesia (a civil-registry /
government services office). The codebase is at F:/hermes/antri-capil. Read files; do not modify
anything. This is analysis only.

Its purpose: citizens book a queue slot online for services (KTP-el, KK, KIA, Pindah Datang, Akta),
get a queue number and a QR ticket, come to the office, and a counter clerk calls them.

=== TASK 1: THE QR CODE IS DEAD WEIGHT. Establish this precisely. ===

The QR is generated in lib/qr.ts and embedded in the email by src/app/api/booking/route.ts
(see the generateQR call around line 75). It encodes `${NEXTAUTH_URL}/tiket/${antrean.id}`.
The ticket page is src/app/tiket/[id]/page.tsx, which re-renders the QR client-side.

Answer with evidence (file:line):
  a) Does ANY code anywhere read, decode, or scan a QR image? Search the whole src/ tree and
     package.json for: a camera/getUserMedia call, BarcodeDetector, html5-qrcode, jsQR,
     qr-scanner, zxing, react-qr-reader, or any file input that accepts an image. Check
     src/app/admin-capil-loket/page.tsx especially.
  b) What is src/app/admin-capil-loket/page.tsx actually? Is it a distinct counter-clerk view or
     does it just re-export the admin page?
  c) Is the QR the only proof of attendance a citizen presents? Trace what actually happens when a
     citizen arrives: is there ANY step where their booking is verified against anything?

=== TASK 2: THE USER FLOW HAS GAPS. Map it, then name the gaps. ===

Map the intended flow from the homepage (src/app/page.tsx advertises it as 4 steps) and the real
routes, then report where reality diverges.

Specifically investigate:
  a) src/app/booking/page.tsx — how is a date chosen? Is it validated client-side againstKuota?
     Does the UI show how many slots remain per day, or only reveal "penuh" after submitting?
  b) src/app/dashboard/page.tsx — a citizen's "Riwayat Saya". Can they cancel a booking? If the
     API has no cancel path for a WARGA, that is a dead end: report it.
  c) src/app/profile/page.tsx — what can a citizen actually change about themselves? Is NIK
     editable? (NIK is the legal identity number; if editable with no verification that is a
     government-regulation problem.)
  d) The admin page (src/app/admin/page.tsx) — is it operable on a phone? Counters in a village
     office use phones/tablets. Look for table-only layouts, hover-only affordances, and
     controls too small for touch.
  e) src/app/display/page.tsx is the TV board. Verify it only reads fields that the current
     authenticated/anonymous projection actually returns. Does it need `waktuPanggil`?

=== TASK 3: VISUAL INCONSISTENCY — THE OWNER SAYS THE UI FEELS UNEVEN. ===

Owner profile: prefers high-contrast, readable text, light mode, modern clean, whitespace-heavy.
The user reports the app "kurang konsisten" (not consistent enough).

There are two colour systems in the codebase. Citizen-facing pages use a teal + warm-cream palette
(`bg-[#FFFBF0]`, `teal-600`, `orange-200`); the admin and display pages use blue + gray + zinc
(`bg-gray-50`, `bg-zinc-900`, `blue-600`). Verify this and list every file on each side.

Report:
  a) The exact colour vocabulary in use — every bg-*, text-*, border-*, rounded-* and
     font-black/bold combination that appears in 3+ files. Where is it genuinely shared, and
     where does a page invent its own shades?
  b) Inconsistencies that a non-developer would notice: mixed background colours between adjacent
     screens, different corner radii for the same kind of element, different button heights,
     different heading sizes, emoji icons used in some places and SVG/blank in others, a page with
     a dark hero and a page with a light hero.
  c) Naming inconsistency: the app is called "AntriCapil" on the homepage, "Antrean Online" on
     the display board, and the footer says "AntriCapil". Confirm and report.
  d) The public URL: the display board advertises "antricapil.go.id" in hardcoded text
     (src/app/display/page.tsx ~line 68) and the booking route falls back to
     "https://antri-capil.vercel.app" for QR links. Flag this as a hardcoded-string problem.

=== TASK 4: WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING FOR A REAL GOVERNMENT OFFICE. ===

Be concrete and prioritise. For a Disdukcapil queue system in Indonesia, which of these are real
gaps rather than nice-to-haves, and what is the smallest useful version of each?
  - Counter clerk verifying the citizen's QR/ticket on arrival (per TASK 1: currently absent)
  - A citizen cancelling or rescheduling
  - Notifying a citizen whose turn is approaching (email exists; SMS/WhatsApp is the norm in
    Indonesia — is anything like it present?)
  - Daily statistics for the head of the office (antrean per layanan, waktu tunggu, jumlah
    terlayani) — is there any aggregate endpoint or page today?
  - Audit trail of who called/finished which ticket, and when
  - Handling a no-show / LEWATI in the data model
  - Print-friendly receipt (src/app/tiket/[id]/page.tsx has print: classes — does it actually
    print usefully?)
  - Operator/loket management: is there any concept of which counter (loket) a service runs at?
  - Data protection: retention of NIK data, and consent at registration

=== OUTPUT FORMAT — plain text, no preamble, no code rewrites. ===
